name: ccz_phase_polynomial_parity_merge_todd
precondition: dv_recon / Toffoli-level IRCircuit with at least two ccz/ccx gates and no non-Clifford rz (rotations == 0): the non-Clifford content is entirely hidden inside ccz/ccx, so the book's rotation-frame rules see nothing to merge (fingerprint: rotations 0, foldable 0). Needs toffoli, hadamard allowed, measurement_free, no ancilla_room needed, qubits <= 20.
identity: Do NOT lower each ccz on its own. Instead expose each ccz as its phase polynomial over F2 parities and merge across gates. (1) Cut the op list at Hadamards into maximal {cx, x, z, s, sdg, t, tdg, cz, ccz}-segments (api.dv.segments / api.phasepoly.labels gives each wire's affine parity label (mask, const) inside a segment). (2) Inside a segment, replace every ccz(a,b,c) by its exact diagonal expansion as a sum over parities: CCZ = exp(i pi/4 * [p_a + p_b + p_c - p_{a^b} - p_{b^c} - p_{a^c} + p_{a^b^c}]) where p_S is the parity of the label masks of the involved wires, i.e. seven Rz(+-pi/4) gates on the parities {a}, {b}, {c}, {a^b}, {b^c}, {a^c}, {a^b^c}; cz(a,b) is likewise exp(i pi/2 * [...]) over {a},{b},{a^b} and contributes only Clifford (pi/2) weight. (3) Accumulate the whole segment as a single phase polynomial: a map from parity mask (plus affine constant sign) to an angle coefficient mod 2pi, adding coefficients of EQUAL parities. Every pair of equal parities with opposite pi/4 sign annihilates (T * Tdg = I), every pair with equal sign fuses into a Clifford S (pi/2) which costs 0 T, and 8 copies vanish. (4) Re-emit: each surviving coefficient that is an odd multiple of pi/4 becomes one T/Tdg conjugated by a CNOT ladder that builds its parity and unbuilds it; coefficients that are multiples of pi/2 become S/Z (free). (5) Before re-emission, apply one round of TODD/third-order-duplicate reduction (Heyfron-Campbell) on the F2 signature matrix of the odd (T-paying) terms: search pairs of columns a,b whose symmetric difference, when added as the F2 vector a+b to every column, reduces the number of odd-weight columns; each successful move removes 2 T. Iterate to a fixed point, deterministically (lexicographic pair order, first improving move). Re-emit the CNOT ladder from the reduced signature matrix. The rewrite is one segment at a time, so the judge prices and verifies each segment replacement independently.
correctness: A Hadamard-free Clifford+T+CCZ circuit on n wires acts as |x> -> e^{i f(A x + c)} |B x + d> with B, A over F2 and f a sum of linear-parity phase terms; this is the standard phase-polynomial normal form (Amy-Maslov-Mosca). The CCZ identity used in (2) is the exact Reed-Muller expansion of the Boolean function x1 x2 x3 as an F2-parity sum: x1 x2 x3 = (x1 + x2 + x3 - (x1^x2) - (x2^x3) - (x1^x3) + (x1^x2^x3))/4 over the integers, hence CCZ = exp(i pi x1 x2 x3) = exp(i pi/4 [sum of the seven signed parities]); each factor is a diagonal Rz on a parity, so all factors commute and the product is order-independent. Equal parities therefore add their angles exactly, with no approximation and no commutation hypothesis beyond staying inside one Hadamard-free segment (where the parity labels are constant functions of the segment input). T * Tdg = I and T^2 = S are exact, so every cancellation and fusion is exact; re-emitting a parity by a CNOT ladder and unbuilding it restores the linear part B exactly, and the leftover linear map is fixed up by the CNOTs already recorded in labels(). TODD's move adds the F2 vector a+b to all columns of the signature matrix; Heyfron-Campbell prove this leaves the induced cubic form (hence the unitary) invariant up to Clifford corrections that are tracked and reapplied, so it is an exact T-count reduction. Everything is Clifford+T on both sides, so the judge's exact D[omega] check on the changed window decides, and no error budget is drawn. Why this is not the floor's phase-gadget fusion: the floor's pauli_frame_rotation_merge / pauli_exponential_commutation_merge operate on ROTATION ops present in the op list, and this circuit has zero rotations - 100% of its 77 T sit inside 11 opaque ccz gates. The content here is the F2-linear/Reed-Muller algebra that only appears once the ccz are expanded, which no rule in the book does; in the ripple-carry adder the compute and uncompute carry Toffolis generate the SAME parities (the carry wire's label is unchanged between them), so their pi/4 terms cancel pairwise instead of each paying 7 T.
trigger: Scan the op list. Fire on each maximal Hadamard-free segment (cut set {h, measure}) that contains >= 2 gates from {ccz, ccx} (ccx(a,b;c) is handled as h(c) ccz(a,b,c) h(c), i.e. its target Hadamards become new segment cuts and are left in place, so only the ccz core enters the polynomial). Guards: the segment's gates are all in {x, z, s, sdg, t, tdg, cx, cz, ccz}; no measurement or classically controlled gate inside; segment touches <= 20 wires. Emit one match per qualifying segment, largest ccz-count first, carrying the segment index range. On adder_6 the 'h ccz h' trigram occurs 11 times and 'cx h ccz' 9 times, so the ccx targets' Hadamards split the circuit; the match set is the segments between them, and after the first merge pass the surviving T-ladders themselves open longer Hadamard-free runs, so the rule is re-triggered to a fixed point.
expected_effect: The 11 ccz expand into 77 signed pi/4 parity terms. In a ripple-carry adder every carry Toffoli is mirrored by an uncompute Toffoli on the same three wires with the same parity labels, and the fingerprint already reports 5 shared_control_pairs; those produce equal parities with opposite effective sign across the pair, so their pi/4 terms either cancel outright or fuse to Clifford S. Counting conservatively: the 5 mirrored pairs contribute ~10 cancelling parity classes out of their 70 terms, and the TODD pass removes a further 2 T per successful column move. Target T 77 -> 47, i.e. matching pyzx's exact-unitary number from a completely different mechanism, with realistic upside below it (published phase-polynomial results on rc_adder_6 sit at 47 for Tpar and lower for TODD-class reduction). No qubits added, CNOT count rises by the parity ladders (bounded by 2 CNOTs per surviving T term); cost order is lexicographic in (T, qubits, CNOT) so the T drop decides.
source: M. Amy, D. Maslov, M. Mosca, 'Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits via matroid partitioning', IEEE TCAD 33(10), 2014, arXiv:1303.2042 (phase-polynomial normal form, parity merging); L. Heyfron, E. Campbell, 'An efficient quantum compiler that reduces T count', Quantum Sci. Technol. 4, 015004 (2019), arXiv:1712.01557 (TODD / third-order duplicate and destroy); Nam, Ross, Su, Childs, Maslov, 'Automated optimization of large quantum circuits with continuous parameters', npj QI 4, 23 (2018) (rc_adder_6 reference counts)
